# Sweep Line Algorithm (SLA)

The sweeping line algorithm (SLA) is an exact frontier dynamic program for MIS. It replaces the processed region by its boundary assignment and the best score compatible with that assignment [@andrist2023hardness].
Fix a processing order $v_1,\ldots,v_n$ of $G=(V,E)$, and write $N(v)$ for the neighbors of $v$. After step $t$, define
$$
P_t=\{v_1,\ldots,v_t\},
\qquad
U_t=V\setminus P_t,
\qquad
B_t=\{u\in P_t:N(u)\cap U_t\neq\varnothing\}.
$$
For each reachable independent subset $S\subseteq B_t$, SLA stores
$$
f_t(S) := \max\left\{ |I|: I\subseteq P_t\text{ is independent and }I\cap B_t=S \right\}.
$$
The subset $S$ is the boundary bit string. If two processed histories
induce the same $S$, only the one with the larger score is retained.

![Refer to @andrist2023hardness](SLA.png)

- Let $v=v_{t+1}$. After processing $v$, Updating new boundary through
$$
B_{t+1} =
\left\{ u\in P_t\cup\{v\}: N(u)\cap\bigl(U_t\setminus\{v\}\bigr)\neq\varnothing \right\}.
$$

Initialize the new table to $-\infty$. For every stored
$S\subseteq B_t$, apply

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{skip }v:\quad
&T_0=S\cap B_{t+1},
&
f_{t+1}(T_0)
&\leftarrow
\max\{f_{t+1}(T_0),f_t(S)\},
\\
\text{select }v:\quad
&T_1=(S\cup\{v\})\cap B_{t+1},
&
f_{t+1}(T_1)
&\leftarrow
\max\{f_{t+1}(T_1),f_t(S)+1\},
\end{aligned}
$$

where the second line is used only if

$$
S\cap N(v)=\varnothing.
$$

This boundary check is sufficient: every processed neighbor of
$v\in U_t$ belongs to $B_t$ by definition.

Intersecting with $B_{t+1}$ forgets every vertex that no longer touches
the future. In Fig. 2, the light-blue vertex enters the boundary and the
lower-left blue vertex leaves it.

The forgotten bit is discarded, but its contribution remains in
$f_t(S)$. If several old states project to the same new state, the
maximum operation keeps only the best history.

:::{.callout-note collapse="true" icon="false"}
## Correctness and cost

The invariant is the definition of $f_t$: it is the largest independent
set in $P_t$ compatible with each boundary state. Initially,
$P_0=B_0=\varnothing$ and $f_0(\varnothing)=0$.

Every independent set in $P_{t+1}$ either excludes or includes $v$,
giving the two transitions above. The inclusion branch is legal exactly
when $S\cap N(v)=\varnothing$.

Vertices removed from the boundary have no neighbors in $U_{t+1}$.
Histories with the same projected boundary state therefore have the same
future extensions, so max-merging cannot remove an optimum.

After the final vertex, $U_n=B_n=\varnothing$, and hence

$$
f_n(\varnothing)=\alpha(G)=|\mathrm{MIS}|.
$$

If $b=\max_t|B_t|$, at most $2^b$ states are stored. The generic memory
cost is $O(2^b)$ and the runtime is
$O(n2^b\operatorname{poly}(b))$.

For the quasiplanar UD instances studied in
@andrist2023hardness, valid boundary states satisfy a Fibonacci bound.
With $N\asymp L^2$, the reported scaling is

$$
O_{\mathrm{mem}}\!\left(\mathrm{Fib}(\sqrt N)\right),
\qquad
O_{\mathrm{time}}\!\left(N\,\mathrm{Fib}(\sqrt N)\right)
\approx O\!\left(N\phi^{\sqrt N}\right).
$$

For MWIS, replace $|I|$ by $w(I)$ and the increment $+1$ by $+w(v)$;
the state space and correctness argument are unchanged.
:::
